[b]Operation Haiyan[/b]

The departure of the isolationist navy would prove to pose somewhat of an issue against Qianxun forces. Since the start of the operation, Qianxun forces have largely limited their naval capabilities to three types of watercraft: A dozen auxiliary surface combat and landing ships created from converted merchant vessels, which had only some basic armaments like twin 25mm/80 guns and a few anti-ship missile launchers; Five [i]Anlan[/i]-class missile boats, which were airlifted from the Qianxun Lakes with the latest in subsonic anti-ship cruise missile technology, MANPAD missiles, and 30mm guns; and last but not least, three amphibious assault ships supplied courtest of SummitONE, the QNS [i]Du Jiao[/i], QNS [i]Tongyi[/i], and QNS [i]Weizhu[/i]. 

Additionally, an experimental fast combat support ship called the [i]Bicang[/i] ("Jade Repository") would be apparently present among Qianxun naval forces, having been spotted by Astaniran locals due to its unusual design and its many, many missions resupplying the Qianxun expeditionary fleet. However, it has been mysteriously absent since the deposition of the Arono government, possibly having been hidden by Qianxun agents at [i]Kuangye Point[/i], the codename for David Cyriacus's [i]ad hoc[/i] central headquarters.

Qianxun forces had no submarines available in Astanir, having initially thought them to be impractical due to the modernized ASW capabilities of the [i]Anlan[/i]-class. However, with doubts now being spread among Pax Int'l's leadership of the effectiveness of their offensives, the order would be given to retain all twenty Qianxun vessels near the Democratic coast under the protection of its coastal batteries. This move, while criticized by some officials for vastly overestimating the capabilities of the isolationist naval force, would nevertheless be accepted without further incident. Admiral Yun Caibo, the [i]de facto[/i] head of all naval forces and architect of this defensive strategy, would in the mean time order retraining to begin on all available Astaniran Democratic naval ships, with Yun hoping to find a few submarines in the Democratic arsenal which might be used to confront the enemy at the sea.

In the mean time, however, with the Tiansheng pocket now resolved and with General Bai He's 5th Maneuver Army having stalled on the frontline, the time was now for the  1st and 2nd Maneuver Armies of SummitONE operational managers Freya Moran and Edwin Roylance to make their appearance. Unlike Bai He's forces, which were predominantly Astaniran,  1st and 2nd Maneuver Armies would be predominatly Vespurian and Qianxun. Well-armed, well-supplied, and well-trained, though in need of experience in the complex Astaniran jungle terrain, Moran and Roylance would launch a gigantic, "hail army" combined arms charge along the western and central salients formed by Bai's offensives.

Anticipating zealous resistance, Moran and Roylance would both organized DEAD campaigns so that Democratic air forces could work in tandem with the Moran-Roylance offensive. During this time, nearly 40% of all Wuying-98 sorties would be identify and destroy isolationist AA units and radar equipment. The antiquated isolationist strategic bombers sent to blunt Pax Int'l forces would have some trouble reaching their targets thanks to interception by Wuying-89s, chiefly due to the weaker capabilities of the bombers' isolationist escorts, but also thanks to Democratic aerial superiority that had been established against the isolationists since the deposition of Haru Arono. 

To maintain tactical cohesion, exhausted and demoralized troops at the very front of the campaign would start to finally be rotated out in favor of elements of Erzhu Qingsheng's 6th Maneuver Army and the fresh Democratic Legionnaires. Additionally, Democratic forces would also begin advising several "peasant warlords" along their offensive campaign to begin setting up soviets with which to facilitate the construction of supply depots, refueling stations, fresh roads, field hospitals and [i]ad hoc[/i] factories to keep advancing Democratic forces well-supplied. 

[b]Operation Julong[/b]

After negotiating a ceasefire with the Argossian militias, Generals Duan Liqin and Tazio Diodati would be remain content with maintaining a stalemate against the restorationists, with this having been their duty in the first place. While some elements within the 3rd and 4th Maneuver Armies would suggest taking the initiative and instigating a dedicated offensive, both generals would opt against this, fearing both court martial by the CEDC and the risk of opening up a second, far more dangerous front. For now, Operation Julong would restrain itself to just a few infantry skirmishes and minor SEAD raids to keep the restorationists on high alert while also dissuading any attempts at an enemy offensive.
